title: In Proverbs 16 What Does It Mean To Commit Our Plans To The Lord And How Can We Practically Do This In Our Daily Lives
paragraphs: Exploring Proverbs 16: Committing Our Plans to the Lord

The wisdom literature of Proverbs offers deep insights into how God desires His people to live wisely and in dependence on Him. One of the central themes in Proverbs 16 is the idea of committing our plans to the Lord. This Bible study explores what it means to entrust our plans to God and how we can put this principle into practice every day.
The Key Passage: Proverbs 16:3
Commit thy works unto Jehovah, and thy purposes shall be established. -
Proverbs 16:3 ASV

The word "commit" in this verse comes from a Hebrew root meaning "to roll." The imagery is of rolling our burdens or plans onto the Lord, entrusting Him with the direction and outcome of our efforts. This is not simply telling God what we intend to do and asking for His blessing, but rather submitting our desires and intentions to His sovereign will.
The Sovereignty of God in Our Plans
Proverbs 16 repeatedly emphasizes God’s sovereignty over human affairs:
The plans of the heart belong to man; But the answer of the tongue is from Jehovah. -
Proverbs 16:1 ASV
A man's heart deviseth his way; But Jehovah directeth his steps. -
Proverbs 16:9 ASV

These verses remind us that while we are responsible to plan wisely, it is ultimately God who determines the outcome. True wisdom recognizes our dependence on God and seeks His guidance and blessing in all things.
Committing Our Plans: Trust and Surrender
Committing our plans to the Lord involves two key attitudes:
Trust – Believing that God is wise, good, and sovereign, and that His ways are higher than ours (Isaiah 55:8-9 ASV).
Surrender – Yielding our will to God’s, willing to accept His direction even when it differs from our own preferences (Luke 22:42 ASV).
Scripture consistently calls us to walk by faith, not by sight (2 Corinthians 5:7 ASV), and to acknowledge God in all our ways:
Trust in Jehovah with all thy heart, And lean not upon thine own understanding: In all thy ways acknowledge him, And he will direct thy paths. -
Proverbs 3:5-6 ASV
Practical Ways to Commit Our Plans to the Lord
But how do we actually do this in everyday life? Here are practical steps:
Begin with Prayer
Before making plans, seek the Lord in prayer, asking for wisdom and clarity. James reminds us:
But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him. -
James 1:5 ASV
Search the Scriptures
Align your plans with God’s revealed will in His Word. God never leads us to do anything contrary to Scripture (Psalm 119:105 ASV).
Seek Godly Counsel
Proverbs encourages seeking wisdom from others:
Where there is no counsel, purposes are disappointed; But in the multitude of counsellors they are established. -
Proverbs 15:22 ASV
Hold Plans Loosely
Make plans, but be willing to adjust or change them if God leads differently. James warns against arrogant confidence in our own plans:
For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall both live, and do this or that. -
James 4:15 ASV
Act in Faith
Once you have prayerfully considered and committed your plans to God, move forward in obedience and trust, knowing that He is able to direct your steps.
Encouragement for Daily Living

Committing our plans to the Lord is not a one-time event but a daily practice of trust and surrender. When we do this, we find peace in knowing that God is at work in every situation, and we can rest in His faithful guidance. As Paul writes:
And we know that to them that love God all things work together for good, even to them that are called according to his purpose. -
Romans 8:28 ASV
Let us, therefore, roll our plans, dreams, and daily decisions onto the Lord, trusting Him to establish our steps and fulfill His perfect will in our lives.
